target_claim: The proof's "Distributing" step claims that from $\paren{\paren{m \vee n} \vee b} \wedge \paren{\paren{n \vee m} \vee a} \in F$ one may conclude $\paren{m \vee n} \wedge \paren{b \vee a} \in F$. This inverts the distributive law: in a distributive lattice $(x \vee b) \wedge (x \vee a) = x \vee (a \wedge b)$, not $x \wedge (a \vee b)$. The two expressions are not equal and the second is not above the first (it is in fact $\le x \le x \vee (a\wedge b)$), so upward closure of the filter does not license the step.
